text: Kingsmoor FC and Westport Albion put on a goal-filled show ending 3-3. Viktor Quinlan sparked Kingsmoor with a confident penalty and a slick team goal early on, showing their wide, crossing play style [#152] [#222]. Westport hit back quickly with two top chances finished by Rafael Delacroix, scoring from neat, quick passes straight towards goal [#401] [#553]. After halftime, Kenji Rahman leveled for Westport, keeping the match tight [#983]. Despite losing Felix Barros to a red card, Kingsmoor didn’t back down and Luca Iversen netted a great late goal from a fast cross, sealing the draw [#1495] [#1516]. Both teams pressed hard but made tactical shifts—Kingsmoor raised their intensity chasing the game, while Westport tried to slow things down and defend their lead [#1187] [#1459]. It was a fantastic battle of styles with plenty of attacking football and drama that left fans on the edge of their seats.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in en

- Viktor Quinlan scored 2 goals early for Kingsmoor FC, including a penalty at 8' with an xG of 0.76 [#152].
- Rafael Delacroix scored twice for Westport Albion in the first half with high xG values of 0.816 and 0.976 [#401, #553].
- Kenji Rahman equalized for Westport Albion at 51' with an xG of 0.705 [#983].
- Luca Iversen scored a late goal at 82' for Kingsmoor FC with an xG of 0.888 to make the score 3-3 [#1516].
- Felix Barros received a second yellow card red card at 81', reducing Kingsmoor FC to 10 men [#1495].

- Kingsmoor FC's first goal was a penalty scored by Viktor Quinlan at 8', indicating a defensive foul or pressing error by Westport Albion early on, showing an initial pressing vulnerability by Westport [#152].
- The second Kingsmoor goal at 12' resulted from a sustained 8-pass build-up over 26 seconds starting from a Kingsmoor regain, reflecting their 4-4-2 wide, crossing play style with patience and ball movement to create chances through wide areas before finishing inside 9 meters [#222].
- Westport Albion responded with two quick goals from well-worked sequences involving 7 and 10 passes respectively, starting from regains and featuring short, direct passing vertical to goal, consistent with their 4-4-2 direct style and exploiting spaces in the defensive setup of Kingsmoor [#401, #553].
- Both teams showed pressing intensity differences: Westport had lower PPDA (5.7 overall, 4.8 in 2H) indicating higher pressing, while Kingsmoor started with high PPDA (12.1 in 1H) and increased press after 65' tactical change to press higher and play more direct, showing tactical adjustments to regain control offensively as they chased the game [#1187].
- Westport's second half drop deeper and slowing tempo after 79' reflects a tactical switch to protect the lead, reducing pressing and line height, trading some possession and attacking threat but gaining defensive solidity, corresponding with a decline in field tilt and box touches in 2H [#1459].
- The late Kingsmoor goal at 82', assisted by a cross after a quick 2-pass build-up post-regain, illustrates their wide, crossing play persevering despite being down a man after the 81' red card to Felix Barros, emphasizing their adaptive play style to create high-quality chances in tight situations [#1516, #1494].
